title: Prefetch + Batching econ workshop w/ Skyline DataWorks
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix/KV caching with a simple cost model applied to Skyline's conversational assistant. Focus on sessionization, prefetch heuristics, and latency vs cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: sandbox run, cost spreadsheet, SOC2 and network details.
action_items: Marina Chen: Share cost-simulator CSV and console recording (due: 2026-11-12)
Ethan Lowe: Provide 1 week sample of request traces + sequence length histogram (due: 2026-11-11)
Darren Park: Send sandbox invite and assign pilot AE (due: 2026-11-10)
Priya Rao: Confirm compliance contacts and SOC2 accountant (due: 2026-11-16)
next_steps: Run 48-hour sandbox with Skyline production sample traffic
Populate cost model with real traces and test prefetch TTLs
Schedule technical deep dive on VPC/on-prem options next week
Redwood to share SOC2 + network connectivity checklist
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-09 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Darren (Redwood AE), Marina (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood SE), Priya (Skyline Head of ML), Ethan (Platform), Samir (CTO), Nina (SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Darren: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, this is Darren from Redwood. quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: hi I'm Priya, Head of ML at Skyline, thanks. we run a conversational assistant across web and mobile, about 1.2M monthly active users.
[00:29] Ethan: Ethan here, platform eng, we host services on a mixed cloud setup, primary GCP with some bare-metal for steady loads.
[00:42] Darren: awesome, goal today is to walk through batching/prefetch recs from Redwood Optimize and run a light cost sensitivity sim with your sample traffic. marina will drive the console demo.
[01:05] Marina: hey all, i'll share my screen, but first quick Q: what's your 95th percentile latency SLO on generate?
[01:18] Priya: we target sub 300 ms for chat responses, but okay to go to 400ms if cost delta is big, our customers care most about consistency.
[01:31] Marina: understood. and typical prompt sizes? tokens?
[01:36] Priya: median 220 tokens, tail to 1k, but majority under 400, conversation context is about 3 turns average.
[01:46] Luis: that helps, since batch efficiency and KV cache hit rate depend heavily on sequence length distribution and session stickiness.
[02:05] [screen share noise, link posted: https://redwood.app/console/demo-logs]
[02:14] Marina: i pulled a quick sim using your anonymized histogram Ethan sent, baseline is hosted model xlarge_quant with default batching 8 and no prefetch. cost per 1k tokens ~ $1.12 in the baseline.
[02:34] Priya: that baseline is in line with our billing today, good.
[02:40] Marina: first lever: adaptive batching — increase batch cap but use latency headroom to batch more when requests queue briefly. in the sim, bumping to batch cap 32 and adaptive window saved ~18% tokens and CPU ops without pushing P95 past 320 ms.
[03:05] Ethan: curious, does adaptive batching add jitter on cold start? some of our endpoints spike with new sessions.
[03:14] Marina: yes slight jitter on the first few requests; we recommended session affinity then prefetch to avoid cold starts.
[03:22] Samir: can you explain prefetch a bit more — i get the idea of fetching KV cache entries ahead but how do you avoid wasted work?
[03:31] Marina: good question. Redwood Optimize looks at session heatmaps and issues prefetch for likely-next prefixes only when probability > threshold. if the prefetch misses in the next N seconds we expire it. we surfaced TTL and hit rate tradeoffs in the sim.
[03:57] Luis: note that Skyline has a lot of short sessions on mobile, prefetch heuristics need shorter TTL to avoid filling cache with one-off prefixes.
[04:12] Priya: that's our primary concern — mobile sessions cause cache churn. what's the sample TTL you used?
[04:19] Marina: we used 45 seconds TTL for mobile-heavy cohorts and 300 seconds for web desktop in the sim; mobile cohort still showed 22% cache hit and net saving 12% tokens.
[04:40] [04:42] Ethan: how are you accounting for KV storage costs? sometimes savings on inference are offset by cache storage ops.
[04:49] Darren: good call — the cost model we shared includes estimated KV lookup cost per 1k ops and storage cost per GB-month; in most of our sims prefetch storage increases were small relative to token savings because entries are small (prefix vectors ~ few KB) and TTLs short.
[05:12] Priya: can we see the sensitivity table?
[05:16] Marina: pulling it up — (shared sheet link) — for TTL x hit rate x batch size we plotted net cost delta, also latency delta.
[05:28] [05:30] Marina: example: for mobile cohort with batch cap 24 + prefetch TTL 45s you see a 14% net cost reduction, P95 +18 ms. for web cohort batch 32 + TTL 300s gives 21% cost reduction, P95 +28 ms.
[05:54] Neil: [misattributed speaker, 'Neil' shows in transcript but not in attendee list] are these numbers assuming quantized kernels?
[06:02] Marina: yes, we used 8-bit quantized path for the sim. if you run fp16 the token cost increases but throughput also changes — we'll attach a variant.
[06:15] Priya: we're also worried about cache consistency across regions — some users hit EU nodes, some NA. how does Redwood handle cross-region cache?
[06:27] Luis: there are two patterns: global prefetched cache replicated via async sync (higher complexity) or region-specific prefetch tuned per region. if data residency prohibits replication we recommend region-local TTL tuning.
[06:45] Ethan: how about private deployment, we may want Private with VPC peering, do prefetches still work?
[06:53] Darren: yes, Redwood Private supports KV cache in your VPC; network egress minimal since it's local. we can provide the connectivity diagram.
[07:05] Priya: can you quickly show the console where we edit prefetch rules?
[07:11] Marina: sure. (screen) here is Optimize -> Prefetch -> cohort rules. you can set heuristics based on last N tokens, user attributes, and confidence threshold.
[07:35] Priya: one more Q — how do you measure quality regressions? if we change batch size or prefetch we want to ensure no drop in response quality.
[07:45] Marina: we tie changes to eval sets and prompt tests; Redwood Optimize can run A/B experiments and evaluate against your golden prompts and metrics. we flagged potential regressions when we tried extremely aggressive prefetch that led to stale context.
[08:05] Samir: that A/B sounds useful — we'll need to know how you snapshot models during canary.
[08:11] Darren: we version pinned models and KV schemas; there is an automated fallback to a compatible variant if a canary fails.
[08:23] [08:25] Marina: moving into a short scenario: we modeled a chat flow with a 4-turn context, 60% repeat prefixes across sessions. baseline average tokens per response 380. with prefix caching + batching we saw tokens drop to ~290.
[08:47] Ethan: that's significant. what's the break-even point when prefetch cost > token savings?
[08:53] Marina: in our sheet column 'breakeven-hit-rate' you can see it: for your cost mix, if hit rate < 7% prefetch costs outweigh savings at TTL 300s; at TTL 60s break-even is ~3%.
[09:16] Priya: ok, so for mobile we should be conservative.
[09:21] Luis: also consider sessionization — pinning users to a worker can improve cache locality and means smaller prefetch TTLs can still be effective. downside is loss of global load balancing flexibility.
[09:38] [09:40] Priya: do you support session affinity in Redwood Dedicated?
[09:44] Darren: yes, Dedicated exposes session affinity policies and can reserve pool slots for hot sessions — we can show expected throughput improvements.
[09:53] Samir: what's the impact on autoscaling? sticky sessions sound like they could force more instances.
[09:59] Marina: we recommend hybrid: keep majority stateless with a hot-worker pool for sticky sessions; autoscaler treats the pool as reserved capacity, so overall autoscaling behavior remains predictable.
[10:14] Ethan: any gotchas on request ordering or KV cache TTL race conditions?
[10:19] Luis: careful with writes to KV in multi-region; we recommend idempotent updates and version tags for cache entries to avoid staleness.
[10:30] Priya: can we simulate a real spike — say marketing event doubles traffic for 2 hours — will prefetch increase cost disproportionately during spike?
[10:39] Marina: it can, but Optimize has burst policies: during spikes we can temporarily lower prefetch aggressiveness and rely more on batching at higher caps; the sim shows that with those rules cost delta is muted and latency stays within SLO.
[11:05] Darren: quick pause — any blockers from compliance? Priya mentioned SOC2 earlier.
[11:12] Priya: we need SOC2 and KMS integration details, plus encryption-at-rest confirmation.
[11:18] Darren: we'll attach SOC2 and KMS guide; Redwood integrates with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated.
[11:26] [11:30] Marina: going deeper into the cost model — we include tokens, model GPU minutes, KV lookups, storage, and a small ops buffer. the sheet lets you switch your unit costs; drop your numbers and it recalculates savings.
[11:48] Ethan: can we feed custom unit costs? yes please.
[11:51] Marina: i'll send the template.
[11:55] [12:00] Priya: small tangent — do you have examples of teams that moved from hosted to dedicated because of these optimizations?
[12:09] Darren: yes, a mid-market fintech moved to Dedicated after reaching steady throughput to reduce unit costs and gain network isolation; we can share an anonymized case study.
[12:20] Samir: good. what about observability — token breakdown per route etc?
[12:26] Luis: Console provides token-level breakdown per route, per model, and you can drill into prefix hit metrics and batch size histograms.
[12:36] Marina: showing console panel — here's a trace where prefetch saved two model calls by hitting KV on the second turn.
[12:49] Priya: nice. any limitations on model types? we use mixed open models and some proprietary fine-tuned weights.
[12:58] Marina: we support most transformer-based models; for proprietary models we recommend bringing them into Dedicated or Private; we can help with kernel selection if you have custom ops.
[13:14] Ethan: i need to raise a network question — if we do Private in our VPC, what's the recommended subnet layout for KV cache?
[13:23] Darren: we'll send a diagram but short answer: colocate KV in same VPC and availability zones as the serving pool; use private routes, no internet egress for KV traffic.
[13:34] [13:36] Priya: how long to ramp a pilot?
[13:39] Darren: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: ingest traces, run sandbox with live traffic sample, tweak Optimize rules, then 1 week of A/B before wider rollout.
[13:50] Priya: timeline aligns with our Q1 plan, good.
[13:55] Marina: moving back to mechanics — prefetch rules can be user-level or route-level. for Skyline we recommended route-level prefetch on high-frequency flows and user-level for logged-in power users.
[14:10] Ethan: are there any security concerns with prefetch storing user PII?
[14:15] Luis: you should avoid caching PII; Redwood Optimize supports filters to strip PII before storing any prefix metadata.
[14:25] Priya: that's mandatory.
[14:28] [14:30] Samir: let's talk numbers: if we go to Dedicated what are the committed capacity tiers?
[14:36] Darren: we have monthly reserved GPU pool sizes with commit discounts; we'll include the pricing sheet in the follow-up. Dedicated also offers SLA on latency.
[14:46] Marina: back to the simulation: i want to show a lower-latency configuration where you keep batch cap low but rely more on KV for token savings. (changes view) here you see P95 < 300ms but token savings ~8% vs 21% when we batch more.
[15:14] Priya: tradeoffs obvious — lower P95 but smaller savings. we need to pick the sweet spot.
[15:19] Ethan: can the console auto-suggest?
[15:22] Marina: yes, Optimize has a recommendations engine that suggests batch cap, prefetch TTL, and cohort splits based on traces, with expected cost/latency deltas. we showed a preview of recommended configs in the sheet.
[15:38] [15:40] Priya: how transparent are the kernels — i mean if something goes wrong we want stack traces and perf counters.
[15:47] Luis: Console exposes traces, kernel-level counters, and per-token timing. for Private we can increase retention of those logs.
[15:58] Samir: any red flags we should test in pilot?
[16:03] Marina: test cache stampede with TTL expiry, region failover, and low hit-rate cohorts — we provide test harnesses in the sandbox.
[16:15] Ethan: ok let's talk about the sandbox run specifics. what instrumentation do we need to provide?
[16:21] Marina: just a week of anonymized traces, a set of golden prompts for evals, and credentials for a service account to push traffic into the sandbox.
[16:31] Priya: we can do that.
[16:34] [16:36] Darren: quick pause — any final technical unknowns?
[16:40] Nina: SRE wonder — how does rolling updates behave with a warm KV? do you lose warm entries?
[16:47] Luis: rolling updates will evacuate workers and KV entries can be re-warmed via prefetch on cold nodes, but there's an expected short window of slightly higher latency. we can run a canary with warmup scripts.
[17:05] Priya: i think that's acceptable if documented.
[17:09] Marina: circling back, i'll attach the console walkthrough video and the cost model CSV.
[17:16] Darren: next steps recap — we'll run 48-hour sandbox, you supply traces, we share SOC2 and pricing.
[17:24] Priya: perfect, thanks both.
[17:28] [17:30] Darren: any competitor concerns? Priya: they are evaluating Vertex AI and Anthropic — main criteria is predictability and total cost of ownership.
[17:43] Darren: noted. Redwood focuses on production controls, we'll highlight that in follow-up.
[17:50] Marina: last thing, i'll drop a short checklist in the chat for sandbox readiness.
[17:55] Ethan: thanks, received.
[18:00] Samir: thanks all.
[18:05] [meeting ends at ~52:00, recording stopped]
recap: Redwood walked Skyline through Optimize recommendations: adaptive batching, prefix/KV prefetch heuristics, TTL tuning, and session affinity. Demoed console panels and shared a cost-simulator. Agreed to a 48-hour sandbox and to exchange traces, SOC2, and pricing. Action items assigned.
